content.overview: BNS s. 68 — Sexual intercourse by a person in authority.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Sexual intercourse by a person in authority. BNS restatement of IPC 376C. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 376C. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 68 is the rule on “Sexual intercourse by a person in authority”. The section provides that whoever, being—. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 68 exists so that “Sexual intercourse by a person in authority” has a closed legal test in Chapter V — Of Offences Against Woman and Child. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Sexual offences, assault, marriage, miscarriage, and offences against the child — placed first among the offence chapters.

The provision in detail
68. Whoever, being—

(a) in a position of authority or in a fiduciary relationship; or

(b) a public servant; or

(c) superintendent or manager of a jail, remand home or other place of custody established by or under any law for the time being in force, or a women’s or children’s institution; or

(d) on the management of a hospital or being on the staff of a hospital,

abuses such position or fiduciary relationship to induce or seduce any woman either in his custody or under his charge or present in the premises to have sexual intercourse with him, such sexual intercourse not amounting to the offence of rape, shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than five years, but which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine

Essential ingredients
1. The accused falls within one of the statutory categories: (a) a position of authority or fiduciary relationship; (b) a public servant; (c) superintendent or manager of a jail, remand home or other place of custody established by or under law, or a women’s or children’s institution; or (d) a person on the management or staff of a hospital.
2. The woman is in the accused’s custody, under his charge, or present in the relevant premises.
3. The accused abuses the relevant position or fiduciary relationship to induce or seduce the woman to have sexual intercourse with him.
4. The sexual intercourse does not amount to the offence of rape; the statutory punishment is rigorous imprisonment for not less than five years, extendable to ten years, and liability to fine.

Explanations
Explanation 1.—In this section, “sexual intercourse” shall mean any of the acts mentioned in clauses (a) to (d) of section 63

Explanation 2.—For the purposes of this section, Explanation 1 to section 63 shall also be applicable

Explanation 3.—“Superintendent”, in relation to a jail, remand home or other place of custody or a women’s or children’s institution, includes a person holding any other office in such jail, remand home, place or institution by virtue of which such person can exercise any authority or control over its inmates

Explanation 4.—The expressions “hospital” and “women’s or children’s institution” shall respectively have the same meanings as in clauses (b) and (d) of the Explanation to sub-section (2) of section 64

hypotheticals.analysis:
Step 1 — Identify the provision. The correct current-law cite is BNS s. 68 (Sexual intercourse by a person in authority), Chapter V — Of Offences Against Woman and Child.
Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:
   (1) (a) in a position of authority or in a fiduciary relationship; or
   (2) (c) superintendent or manager of a jail, remand home or other place of custody established by or under any law for the time being in force, or a women’s or children’s institution; or
   (3) (d) on the management of a hospital or being on the staff of a hospital,
   (4) abuses such position or fiduciary relationship to induce or seduce any woman either in his custody or under his charge or present in the premises to have sexual intercourse with him, such sexual intercourse not amounting to the offence of rape, shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than five years, but which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine
Step 3 — Read every Explanation. An explanation is part of the section. Omitting it leaves the analysis incomplete and vulnerable to rebuttal.
Step 4 — Map each fact to an ingredient. Write “this fact proves ingredient (a)” or “this fact is missing, so the section is not made out”.
Step 5 — Conclude. If every essential ingredient is proved and no exception covers the case, BNS s. 68 applies. If any essential ingredient fails, say so and stop. Do not invent a different section to save the answer.

learningObjectives: Understand custodial sexual exploitation under BNS s. 68.
Analyze the categories of authority: superintendents of jails, remand homes, hospitals, and educational institutions.
Examine the misuse of official position inducing or seducing a woman in custody/care.
enhancement.definition: BNS s. 68 provides that whoever, being in a position of authority or in a fiduciary relationship, or being a public servant, or being a superintendent or manager of a jail, remand home or other place of custody or shelter established by or under any law, or hospital, takes advantage of his official position to induce or seduce any woman in his custody or under his care or charge, or any patient, to have sexual intercourse with him, such sexual intercourse not amounting to the offence of rape, shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than five years, but which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Persons in institutional or custodial power over vulnerable women cannot exploit their official authority to obtain sexual access. Even if physical violence is absent and superficial consent was procured through institutional leverage, the law penalizes it as custodial sexual exploitation.
statutoryFramework: Chapter V — Of Offences against Women and Children, BNS s. 68 (corresponding to IPC s. 376C).
Actors: Public servants, persons in authority/fiduciary relationship, jail/remand home superintendents, hospital managers.
Modus operandi: Takes advantage of official position to 'induce or seduce'.
Victims: Women in custody, under care or charge, or hospital patients.
Condition: 'such sexual intercourse not amounting to the offence of rape'.
Penalty: Rigorous imprisonment from five to ten years and fine.
essentialIngredients: The accused falls within a statutory category in BNS s. 68: (a) a position of authority or fiduciary relationship; (b) a public servant; (c) superintendent or manager of a jail, remand home or other place of custody established by or under law, or a women’s or children’s institution; or (d) a person on the management or staff of a hospital.
The woman is in the accused’s custody, under his charge, or present in the relevant premises.
The accused abuses the relevant position or fiduciary relationship to induce or seduce the woman to have sexual intercourse with him.
The sexual intercourse does not amount to the offence of rape; assess that statutory boundary separately under the applicable facts and law.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 68 protects women trapped in institutional custody where real free consent is an illusion. An inmate in a women's shelter home, a prisoner in a jail, or an impoverished patient in a government hospital is completely dependent on institutional managers for food, basic care, medical releases, or parole. If a superintendent uses his administrative authority to induce a female inmate into sexual relations—promising better food, early release, or threatening solitary confinement—s. 68 criminalizes the act. The law recognizes that institutional leverage destroys genuine voluntariness.
examples: Teaching example (Shelter home superintendent): The superintendent of a state shelter home for destitute women promises an inmate extra rations and family visits if she engages in sexual relations with him. She submits reluctantly. Section 68 applies; the superintendent faces 5 to 10 years RI.

Teaching example (Hospital doctor and patient): A senior doctor in an inpatient psychiatric ward uses his clinical authority over a vulnerable patient to induce sexual intercourse. Section 68 protects the patient and penalizes the doctor.
distinctions: Section 68 vs Section 64(2) (Aggravated custodial rape): Section 64(2) applies when force or non-consent is present (rape, minimum 10 years to natural life); Section 68 applies when institutional leverage induced submission without overt rape (5 to 10 years).
Fiduciary exploitation vs Consensual adult relationship: Section 68 requires proof that the accused took advantage of his official position.
problemApplication: Issue: What is the liability of a remand home superintendent who engaged in sexual intercourse with an adult female inmate after promising to favorably recommend her discharge?
Rule: Under BNS s. 68, a person in authority who takes advantage of his position to induce or seduce a woman in his custody is liable to 5 to 10 years RI.
Application: The accused was the official superintendent and utilized discharge leverage to induce submission.
Conclusion: The superintendent is convicted under s. 68.
